newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures rallied with other bond markets after U.S. economic data calmed fears of an imminent interest rate rise but analysts said the market would remain prudent ahead of more key U.S. data later this week.
The March bond future was hoisted out of negative territory after U.S. bonds surged, mainly on relief, as the U.S. fourth quarter employment cost index came in roughly in line with expectations.
"The numbers came in as expected and we had a rebound because the market had got a bit scared," Nathalie Fillet, bond analyst at Banque Paribas, said.

An economist at a French mutual fund manager said the bond future should continue to climb towards 131 but there was a risk it would not be able to get through that level ahead of the publication of U.S. fourth quarter gross domestic product. "If there weren't GDP on Friday, we would climb more," he said.
The contract hit a low of 129.76 earlier and then rallied to reach a high of 130.70. A rise in U.S. consumer confidence in January stalled the climb and the contract settled at 130.50.
He said European bonds could also underperform U.S. bonds in the event of a rally as European yields were currently so far below U.S. yields.

Joanne Perez, strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris, was sceptical about how much further the declines in yields could go. She said she thought the French market was ripe for a correction, "Real yields are terribly low historically. I think 6.50 (percent) should be more the objective rather than 5.50."

She also said the fact that French domestic investors were looking to overseas bond markets to pick up yield suggested convergence trades had gone too far. "We can expect a 10 basis points narrowing of the spread," she said.
The yield on the October 2006 OAT fell to 5.57 percent on Tuesday, 19 basis points below equivalent German bond yields.
Traders said March PIBOR reversed some of its recent losses at the end of the session as a U.S. fund became a buyer again after selling steadily for several days to take profits.

"We had a good day. We broke support in the morning at 96.70 and fell to 96.67 after stops were triggered and then climbed to 96.75 which was clearly too high bearing in mind the low for the day," a PIBOR trader at a U.S. house said.

Several traders said they regretted missing out on the rally at the end of the session as the contract was at a good level to buy. They said it now had the potential to climb further but would struggle to reach its all-time high of 96.83.
